title: Monodromy and tensor of modules descended along a finite Galois cover
statement:
Let $S$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $c:T\to S$ be a connected finite etale Galois cover [def-galois-object] with finite group $G=\operatorname{Aut}_S(T)$, let $\bar t$ be a geometric point of $T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], put $\bar s=c\circ\bar t$ and $\Pi=\pi_1(S,\bar s)$ with its profinite topology [def-galois-fibre-functor], and let $R$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $n>0$. For an $R$-module $V$ with an $R$-linear $G$-action $\rho$, let $T_{c,R}(V)$ be the $R_S$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of [lem-per-galois-cover-module-descent], obtained by descending the constant sheaf $V_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] along $c$, together with its trivialization $c^{-1}T_{c,R}(V)\cong V_T$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Stalks are geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and $(c^{-1}F)_{\bar t}$ is identified with $F_{\bar s}$. Local systems and their monodromy actions are those of [lem-per-torsion-local-system-monodromy]. Then:

1. *(Monodromy of a descended module.)* There is a continuous surjective group homomorphism $\theta:\Pi\to G$ with kernel $c_*\pi_1(T,\bar t)$, depending only on $c$ and $\bar t$ (not on $R$ or $V$), with the following property. For every such $(V,\rho)$ the sheaf $T_{c,R}(V)$ is a local system, and the map $\gamma_V:V\to T_{c,R}(V)_{\bar s}$ sending $v$ to the germ at $\bar t$ of the constant section $v$ of $c^{-1}T_{c,R}(V)\cong V_T$ is an $R$-linear isomorphism, natural in equivariant linear maps, with $g\cdot\gamma_V(v)=\gamma_V(\rho(\theta(g))v)$ for the monodromy action of every $g\in\Pi$.
2. *(Tensor of descended modules.)* For two such $(V,\rho)$ and $(W,\sigma)$ there is an isomorphism of $R_S$-module sheaves
$$T_{c,R}(V)\otimes_{R_S}T_{c,R}(W)\cong T_{c,R}(V\otimes_RW)$$
[def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], where $G$ acts on $V\otimes_RW$ by $g(v\otimes w)=\rho(g)v\otimes\sigma(g)w$, natural in $V$ and $W$, whose pullback along $c$ sends the tensor $v\otimes w$ of the constant sections $v$ of $V_T$ and $w$ of $W_T$ to the constant section $v\otimes w$ of $(V\otimes_RW)_T$.

No finiteness of $R$, $V$ or $W$ and no flatness is assumed.

source.place: Section 03SF (pione-section-finite-etale-under-galois): Galois covers correspond to finite quotients $\pi_1(X,\bar x)\to G$ with open normal kernel; Section 0BMQ (pione-section-galois), Lemma 0BN2 (lemma-galois); with ILO, Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3 and its proof, p. 301 (literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf): the fibre of a local system with the action of $\pi_1$ through the equivalence of finite etale covers with finite $\pi_1$-sets, passed to ind-objects; tensor clause: literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex, Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) applied to the descent data.

proof.text: Work with small representatives in a universe containing all the sites and coefficients [def-weil-size-convention]. By clauses (a),(b) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-degree], the finite etale map $c$ has a constant degree $d$ and every geometric fibre has $d$ points. The chosen $\bar t$ shows $d>0$, so $c$ is surjective and is a singleton covering in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] its slice is $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, and likewise for the overlaps. Use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] to identify $c^{-1}F$ with restriction $F|_T$; naturality with respect to each constant scalar makes this identification $R$-linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction], constants restrict to constants with the same unit sections, also on every overlap. These identifications will be used below.

source.place: Tag 00XZ (localization), Tag 00XR (restriction); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03SH (constant finite etale degree).

proof.text: The finite etale category with its geometric fibre is a Galois category by [lem-fet-galois-category], and $T$ is a connected object by [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object]. Thus [lem-galois-transitive] gives transitivity of $\Pi$ on $|T_{\bar s}|$. The deck group $G$ acts simply transitively by [def-galois-object]. For $g\in\Pi$, define $a_g\in G$ uniquely by $g\bar t=a_g\bar t$. Naturality in [def-galois-fibre-functor] gives $g(a\bar x)=a(g\bar x)$ for every deck map $a$. Consequently $(gh)\bar t=a_h a_g\bar t$, so $a_{gh}=a_h a_g$. Put $\theta(g)=a_g^{-1}$. Then $\theta(gh)=\theta(g)\theta(h)$ and $\theta(1)=1$. Transitivity gives surjectivity. The orbit map $g\mapsto g\bar t$ is continuous into the finite discrete fibre; the bijection $a\mapsto a\bar t$ and inversion show $\theta$ is continuous. Its kernel is the stabilizer of $\bar t$, identified with $c_*\pi_1(T,\bar t)$ by the finite-etale clause of [thm-galois-fundamental]. This construction uses only $c,\bar t$.

source.place: Section 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois), Section 0BMQ (section-galois), Lemma 0BN3 (lemma-tame); Theorem 0BND for the finite-etale fibre equivalence.

proof.text: Write $L=T_{c,R}(V)$ and $e_V:L|_T\xrightarrow{\sim}V_T$ for its descent trivialization [lem-per-galois-cover-module-descent]. Since $c^{-1}L$ is constant, the converse finite-etale-locality clause of [lem-per-torsion-local-system-monodromy] makes $L$ a local system. Let $s_v=e_V^{-1}(v)\in L(T)$, where $v$ is the global constant section. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], the map $v\mapsto\operatorname{germ}_{\bar t}(v)$ is an isomorphism on underlying abelian groups; it commutes with every scalar $r$ because both constants and germs commute with the map $v\mapsto rv$. Taking the stalk of $e_V^{-1}$ and using the stalk identification stipulated in the statement therefore gives the $R$-linear isomorphism $\gamma_V(v)=\operatorname{germ}_{\bar t}(s_v)$. For an equivariant map $f:V\to V'$, its descended morphism restricts to the constant map $f$, so it takes $s_v$ to $s_{f(v)}$. Taking germs proves the asserted naturality.

source.place: Expose XVII, 7.2.1--7.2.4, pp. 301--302; constant stalk map: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04FM.

proof.text: Unpack descent of the given left $G$-action using the convention $\phi:p_1^{-1}V_T\to p_2^{-1}V_T$. On a graph $(\mathrm{id},a):T\to T\times_ST$ it is the constant map $\rho(a)$; on $(x,ax,bax)$ its cocycle equation is precisely $\rho(ba)=\rho(b)\rho(a)$. Thus the gluing convention $e_2=\phi e_1$ of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent], applied to the descent in [lem-per-galois-cover-module-descent], says that the trivialization on the object $(T,a)$ of $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ is $\rho(a)e_V$ on its canonically identified domain $L(T)$. Naturality of $e_V$ along $a:(T,a)\to(T,\mathrm{id})$, and restriction of constant sections, give $\rho(a)e_V(L(a)s_v)=v$, hence $L(a)s_v=s_{\rho(a)^{-1}v}$. For $g\in\Pi$, apply [lem-per-local-system-finite-cover-germ-action] to $U=T$ and $s_v$ to obtain $g\gamma_V(v)=\operatorname{germ}_{a_g\bar t}(s_v)$. In the defining stalk colimit [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], restriction along $a_g$ identifies this germ with $\operatorname{germ}_{\bar t}(L(a_g)s_v)$. It equals $\gamma_V(\rho(a_g)^{-1}v)=\gamma_V(\rho(\theta(g))v)$, as required. This also explains the inverse in Step 2.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301 (ind-finite monodromy); sites.tex Tags 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves) and 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps), cocycle convention.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ to the constant ring presheaf $R$ and the constant module presheaves $V,W$. Their presheaf tensor is the constant presheaf $V\otimes_RW$, so it gives a natural isomorphism $V_T\otimes_{R_T}W_T\xrightarrow{\sim}(V\otimes_RW)_T$. The comparison sends each tensor of constant sections to the constant section of its tensor: both maps are induced by the same bilinear map $(v,w)\mapsto v\otimes w$ before sheafification. Combine this with [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] and the trivializations $e_V,e_W$ to trivialize $(L\otimes_{R_S}M)|_T$ by $(V\otimes_RW)_T$, where $M=T_{c,R}(W)$. The restriction comparison has the same pure-tensor normalization. Neither comparison assumes finite generation or flatness.

source.place: Tags 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) and 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), specialized to constant presheaves and localized restriction.

proof.text: The graphs $(\mathrm{id},a)$ give the entire double overlap, not just selected geometric points. Indeed, form $q:\coprod_{a\in G}T\to T\times_ST$ with these graph components. These are finite etale $S$-objects by [lem-fet-finite-limits]. On the fibre at $\bar s$, the map is $(a,x)\mapsto(x,ax)$, a bijection by the simple transitivity of [def-galois-object]. By [lem-fet-galois-category] and [def-galois-category], the fibre functor preserves the finite coproduct and product and reflects isomorphisms; hence $q$ is an isomorphism. A triple overlap has components $(x,ax,bax)$, whose pair labels are $a,b,ba$. Thus equality of descent maps may be checked on these graphs, and the cocycle for a left action has the multiplication order used in Step 4.

source.place: Section 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois); Tag 0BNB (lemma-finite-etale-connected-galois-category), exact conservative fibre functor; Tag 0BMY (definition-galois-category).

proof.text: On a double overlap the canonical descent datum of $L\otimes M$ is the tensor of the canonical data of $L,M$: this follows by naturality of the restriction comparison in [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction]. Under Step 5 it sends $v\otimes w$ to $\rho(a)v\otimes\sigma(a)w$ on every graph $(\mathrm{id},a)$. The graphs exhaust the overlap by Step 6. The linear map $\rho(a)\otimes\sigma(a)$ is invertible and respects products of $a$, by evaluation on pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Hence this is exactly the diagonal-action datum defining $T_{c,R}(V\otimes_RW)$. The local comparison and its inverse agree with those data on pure tensors; this checks all sections, since sheaf tensors are sheafified sectionwise tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By the morphism-gluing clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] they descend to mutually inverse maps. The maps are $R_S$-linear since that equality can be checked on the cover, and their composites are identities by gluing uniqueness. The same uniqueness descends the naturality squares in equivariant maps $f,h$, checked locally by $(f\otimes h)(v\otimes w)=f(v)\otimes h(w)$. Step 5 gives precisely the requested pullback normalization.
